objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a young adult patient presenting with altered mental status, suspected of having a serious drug reaction.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Doctor: “Hello—what brings you in today?” Patient: “I… don’t understand. I’m not answering questions.” Doctor: “You’re very unwell—do you recognize where you are?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: Can you tell me when you first noticed that you were feeling confused or not recognizing where you are?
“I can’t answer that—I don’t understand what you’re asking.” “I don’t recognize where I am, and I’m not able to respond normally.”
Doctor: Have you had any recent fever, chills, headache, or a feeling of being “sick” before this confusion started?
“Yes—there’s been a very high fever, around 40°C, and I felt very unwell before things got worse.” “My muscles feel stiff and I’m breathing and heart rate feel fast, but I can’t properly explain it.”
Doctor: Do you have any neck stiffness or pain when you try to move your head, or does looking at bright lights make you uncomfortable?
“No neck stiffness that I can tell you about… and bright lights don’t really feel different to me.” “I feel very hot, my muscles are very stiff, and I’m having trouble responding.”
Doctor: Have you taken any new medications or substances in the past few days—such as antibiotics, antipsychotics, antidepressants, over‑the‑counter drugs, or recreational drugs?

“I haven’t taken anything new that I can clearly say, but I do have a recent history of using substances and I might have taken something again.” “I’m not cooperative and I can’t keep track of what it was right now.” “I just feel extremely hot, with stiff muscles and I’m not responding normally.”
Doctor: In the past few days, have you taken any antipsychotic or dopamine‑blocking medications (for example, haloperidol, risperidone, quetiapine, metoclopramide, or similar drugs)?

“I don’t know—I can’t say what I took or whether anything like that was involved.” “I just remember being very hot with stiff muscles and not responding normally.” “I refuse to keep answering questions.”

Doctor: In the last 24 hours, have you noticed worsening sweating or a dry mouth, and have you been able to urinate normally? Patient: “I’m extremely hot, my mouth feels very dry, and I can’t say if I’m urinating normally—I’m not able to cooperate.” Doctor: Are you currently feeling stiff all over, or is it mainly in your limbs? Patient: “Stiff all over—my muscles feel rigid, and I can’t respond the way you’re asking.”
Doctor: In the past 24 hours, have you been in a very hot environment—such as outdoors in extreme heat, a sauna, or a crowded indoor space—where you might have been unable

“Yes—I was outdoors in extremely hot weather and I ended up undressing. I’ve been very hot since then, with dry mouth, fast heartbeat, and muscle stiffness, and I’m not able to answer questions reliably.”
